summary: Kimama Butte lookout: 14x14 ft cab with trailer quarters in 1937, new cab in 1975, destroyed 2003; radio towers now on the summit.

facts.design: 14x14 ft cab with trailer quarters (1937); new cab 1975
facts.status_note: Destroyed 2003; the summit now carries radio towers and no source describes remains of the cab

staffing.status: Named keepers in 1958, 1962 and 1970; the climbing guide says manned in summers to 1975

access.note: BLM land; SummitPost says entrance is unrestricted. No source describes public access to the tower area itself.

visit.trail_note: 2-track road climbs toward the summit; steep and rocky near the top; SummitPost advises a high-clearance vehicle

events.note: Range fire on the butte between Paul and Kimama; lookouts reported it still not under control; about 100 acres burned
Station not manned for lack of appropriations
Lightning bolt within 50 feet of the station started a 4,000-acre range fire in Lincoln County
Walter Chapman, keeper at the station
Boyd Walton and wife spent the summer at the station
Bob Locke and wife keep a regular fire watch; last named keeper in the sources
Destroyed; climbing guide says demolished in the early 2000s

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The climbing guide says summers 1937 to 1975; SummitPost says 1937 to at least 1970; the named keepers in Forest Lookouts end with Bob Locke in 1970, and the 1975 new cab is reported separately. The story gives 1970 as the last named keeper and reports the 1975 cab on its own.
firelookout.com and Forest Lookouts date the loss to 2003; the climbing guide says demolished in the early 2000s. The story uses 2003.

notes_for_editor: Idaho Fire Lookouts (southern-idaho page) agrees on the 1937 cab, the 1975 new cab and the 2003 loss, but was not quoted because its page text has special characters. A 1940 Forest Lookouts item about Baldy Butte near Paul is a different site and was left out. The 1950 NGS description covers the house only and does not say what survives. Keeper names from firelookout.com's longer 1945-1970 list were not used beyond the three quoted from Forest Lookouts.
